sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Genesis**: The League was formed in **Dhaka** (December 1906) following the **Simla Deputation** (October 1906) led by **Aga Khan III** to Viceroy Minto.
• **Primary Objective**: To promote among Muslims a feeling of loyalty to the British Government and to protect/advance the political rights of Muslims.
• **Ideological Shift**: Transitioned from the Aligarh Movement's focus on education/loyalty to active political lobbying for **Separate Electorates**.
• **Key Metric**: The League's formation was facilitated by the British administration to counter the growing influence of the Indian National Congress (INC) and the Swadeshi Movement.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Led by Aga Khan III; met Viceroy Minto at Simla.
Demand for separate electorates and representation based on political importance.
Prelims: First formal demand for communal representation.
Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka; AIML formally established.
Reaction to the anti-partition agitation and Congress's dominance.

items.definition: A system where only Muslims could vote for Muslim candidates, institutionalized by the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) as a direct result of League lobbying.
The initial policy of the League to remain aloof from the anti-British agitation (Swadeshi) to secure government patronage.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Political Lobbying**: Successfully secured the 'Separate Electorate' provision in the 1909 Morley-Minto Reforms.
• **Institutional Growth**: Established branches across India to consolidate Muslim political opinion.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Internal friction between pro-British loyalists and younger, radicalized nationalists (e.g., Maulana Azad, Jinnah).
• **Solutions**: Eventual shift toward the Lucknow Pact (1916) to align with the Congress against British colonial rule.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-A-D' (Simla, Aga Khan, Dhaka).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Simla Deputation (Oct) -> Aga Khan III (Leader) -> Dhaka (Dec) Formation.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Simla Deputation' (1906) with the 'Simla Conference' (1945). The former was for separate electorates; the latter was for the Wavell Plan.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Institutionalized Communalism' to describe the League's impact on the Indian political landscape.

keyTakeaways: The League was a product of both internal Muslim elite aspirations and British 'Divide and Rule' policy.
The demand for separate electorates was the most significant outcome of the 1906 movement.
The League's initial loyalist stance evolved into a more assertive political force by 1916.
